headline: 18-year-old builds AI study app Aveliq for Nigerian students
summary: Self-taught developer George Erubami created Aveliq, an AI-powered study companion with a five-provider AI chain.
details: George Erubami, an 18-year-old self-taught developer from Ibadan, Nigeria, built Aveliq, an AI-powered study companion. The app uses a five-provider AI chain called GEOCODE Intelligence to ensure fast and reliable performance.

Aveliq's frontend is built with HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript, while the backend uses Node.js with Express and is deployed on Render. The app also uses Firebase Firestore and Firebase Authentication for database and auth purposes.

The app features a unique AI fallback chain, which tries multiple AI providers in sequence to ensure that users receive a response. Aveliq also includes a sliding window rate limiter to prevent abuse.

Aveliq is a Progressive Web App with offline support, allowing users to access cached content even without an internet connection. The app offers a free tier with daily limits, as well as premium subscriptions starting at ₦1,500/month.
Erubami built Aveliq entirely on Android using Termux, Acode, and GitHub, showcasing the possibility of developing complex apps on mobile devices.
caption:
Can an 18-year-old build a cutting-edge AI study app? Meet George Erubami, the self-taught developer behind Aveliq!

George Erubami, an 18-year-old self-taught developer from Ibadan, Nigeria, built Aveliq, an AI-powered study companion. The app uses a five-provider AI chain called GEOCODE Intelligence to ensure fast and reliable performance.

Aveliq's frontend is built with HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript, while the backend uses Node.js with Express and is deployed on Render. The app also uses Firebase Firestore and Firebase Authentication for database and auth purposes.

The app features a unique AI fallback chain, which tries multiple AI providers in sequence to ensure that users receive a response. Aveliq also includes a sliding window rate limiter to prevent abuse.

Aveliq is a Progressive Web App with offline support, allowing users to access cached content even without an internet connection. The app offers a free tier with daily limits, as well as premium subscriptions starting at ₦1,500/month.

Erubami built Aveliq entirely on Android using Termux, Acode, and GitHub, showcasing the possibility of developing complex apps on mobile devices.
